transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-11-19 15:00 UTC | Duration: 46m | Auto-recorded by Fireflies
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Sarah Patel (Helios, Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (Helios, Platform Eng), Olivia Grant (Helios, Security).

Summary: Quick discovery focused on reliability, multi-region failover, and incident-tolerance expectations. Customer wants clarification on Hosted vs Dedicated tradeoffs for graceful degradation, cross-region replication, and SLA commitments plus auditability requirements. Agreed to run benchmarks and share SLA artifacts and pricing.

Topics: reliability goals, fallback topologies, regional routing, SLA definitions, security/audit needs, pilot next steps.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have about 45 minutes. Quick intros?
[00:08] Sarah Patel: Sure, Sarah here, Head of ML at Helios, we build forecasting models for energy markets, main concern is inference availability and data residency when models are used in EU.
[00:16] Liam O'Connor: Liam, platform eng, I'll be owning rollout, orchestration, network stuff.
[00:19] Olivia Grant: Olivia, security and compliance, will surface SOC2/ISO needs and encryption questions.
[00:24] Maya Chen: Great, Diego and I are with Redwood, I'm AE, Diego's our SE, he'll run through technical bits.
[00:29] Diego Alvarez: Hey all, quick note — we usually talk through routing and fallback topologies, then map to Hosted/Dedicated/Private options.

[02:03] Diego Alvarez: Can you describe your tolerance for partial degradation? For example, if a region is down, do you accept higher latency to route to another region, or do you prefer returning a degraded response (like a cached embedding) immediately?
[02:17] Sarah Patel: Good question. For pricing signals and short-cadence models we need latency under 200ms 95th, but for batch scoring it's fine if it runs slower. During outages, product can show degrade, but we need deterministic behavior.
[02:33] Liam O'Connor: Our desire is automatic failover to another region but we want to avoid cross-border data egress when PII is involved. So routing policy must be region-aware, and we need per-tenant routing rules.

[04:10] Maya Chen: On the platform, we support policy-based routing — you can prefer same-region, then same-continent, then global. We also have model variants and quantized fallbacks that are smaller and cheaper — you can degrade to them automatically.
[04:26] Olivia Grant: When you say "model variants" do you mean different checkpoints or like distilled models? Need to know for audit and explainability.
[04:33] Diego Alvarez: Both. Usually a smaller checkpoint or a quantized variant. We'll label them in the catalog; fallbacks carry metadata so you can track which variant served a request for logging.

[06:01] Sarah Patel: Is that metadata included in the audit logs and retained for how long? Our compliance asks for 12 months of request-level auditability.
[06:12] Maya Chen: Yes, we surface token-level logs and model variant IDs in the request trace. For Hosted we have a default retention — 90 days — but enterprise Dedicated/Private supports longer retention and export to your SIEM.
[06:28] Olivia Grant: Export how? S3, Pub/Sub? We need to see encryption-in-transit and at-rest details.
[06:34] Diego Alvarez: S3 transfer is supported, plus direct syslog and streaming to Kinesis. All transfers support TLS 1.2/1.3 and at-rest uses customer-managed keys in Dedicated/Private.

[08:15] Liam O'Connor: On network topology: if we point traffic to Redwood Hosted in eu-west-1 and it loses an AZ, what's the failover chain? Is it another AZ first or do you cross-region?
[08:30] Diego Alvarez: We prefer AZ failover inside a region. If region-level capacity is impacted, routing policies can fail over to a warm region. For Hosted customers we have multi-region redundancy across major clouds — but Dedicated gives you pinned capacity and easier capacity guarantees.

[10:09] Sarah Patel: SLA expectations — do you publish latency SLAs or uptime per model? Our procurement wants numeric guarantees.
[10:18] Maya Chen: For Hosted, we publish platform-level availability targets and best-effort latency goals. Dedicated offers contractual SLAs with uptime and tail-latency targets tied to reserved pools. We can provide an SLA matrix as part of the pricing packet.
[10:36] Olivia Grant: Can SLAs include penalties / credits for failed failovers or extended degradation windows?
[10:42] Maya Chen: Yes, enterprise contracts include service credits. We'll include example terms.

[12:50] Liam O'Connor: Regarding caching — you mentioned K-V cache earlier in docs. Do you do prefix caching and is it safe for multi-tenant use? We want to ensure no data leakage across tenants.
[13:03] Diego Alvarez: We do prefix/KV caching but it's tenant-scoped. For shared hosts we partition eviction and keys. In Dedicated and Private, you can opt out of caching entirely as a policy.
[13:18] Sarah Patel: Good. Also, how long is the warm state for KV? If a regional warm cache is lost and we route to another region, how expensive is cold-start?
[13:27] Diego Alvarez: Cold-start cost depends on sequence length and KV size; we surface metrics for expected token throughput and warm hit ratios. For latency-sensitive endpoints we recommend warm pools in each region.

[15:58] Olivia Grant: On data residency: if a EU tenant's requests accidentally route to US region during failover, do you mask or redact inputs? That's a blocker for us.
[16:12] Maya Chen: We have routing policies that enforce strict residency — failover can be configured to only within EU. If you allow cross-region, we can also add field-level redaction rules but that requires integration on your side to mark sensitive fields.

[18:45] Sarah Patel: How does rollout and canary work with fallbacks? For example, if we deploy a new model in EU only, will US traffic get the old one? We want deterministic routing by model version.
[18:58] Diego Alvarez: Rollouts are versioned per-region; you can set canary percentages per route. Global routing respects pinned model versions and only falls back to compatible variants when primary is unavailable.

[21:10] Liam O'Connor: Benchmarks — we want a 95th percentile token latency baseline and then to test cross-region failover cost. Can you run benchmarks against our sample dataset?
[21:23] Diego Alvarez: Yes, we can run a dedicated benchmark run as part of a pilot on a dedicated pool. We'll need a non-production dataset and an S3 bucket or sample payloads.

[22:47] Maya Chen: Quick qualification: timeline and stakeholders for a pilot?
[22:53] Sarah Patel: We're aiming for a pilot in Dec. Procurement needs a security review first. Timeline: security review now, pilot in early December, production pilot Jan if results are good.

[24:05] Olivia Grant: For security review, we'll need SOC2 Type II, pen-test summary, network diagrams, and details on key management. Also, who has access to keys?
[24:16] Diego Alvarez: We'll share SOC2 artifacts via NDA process; Dedicated/Private supports customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM and RBAC that maps to your SSO. We'll include a diagram.

[26:33] Sarah Patel: One more question — in an incident where capacity is exhausted, do you surge auto-scale and how does that impact latency/billing? We worry about runaway costs during incidents.
[26:45] Diego Alvarez: We have controlled autoscaling and burst policies. For Hosted we may throttle or route to smaller variants; Dedicated gives you reserved headroom plus burst options. Billing can be capped at your commit level; we'll show policy controls to limit spend during incidents.

[29:02] Liam O'Connor: Do you support routing by tenant-level SLAs? e.g., premium tenants get cross-region failover, standard tenants are region-restricted.
[29:12] Maya Chen: Yes, routing policies are per-route or per-tenant. The console exposes per-tenant SLOs and can enforce different fallbacks.

[31:00] Sarah Patel: Are there any known gotchas with private deployments — like limited GPU families in certain regions that might force model changes?
[31:12] Diego Alvarez: On-prem/Private can be constrained by hardware. We provide a compatibility matrix and quantization suggestions. If a region lacks a GPU family, we recommend a smaller quantized variant or CPU fallback with degraded latency.

[33:30] Olivia Grant: Can audit logs be pushed real-time to our SIEM for incident investigations?
[33:38] Diego Alvarez: Yes, streaming to your SIEM is supported and we can set retention and redaction policies.

[35:50] Maya Chen: Let's recap and next steps. We'll send the following: SLA and redundancy playbook, Dedicated pricing with pilot template, SOC2 artifact transfer instructions, and a benchmarking kickoff doc.
[36:03] Sarah Patel: Sounds good. For the deep-dive we'll have Liam + Diego coordinate on dataset and scope.
[36:10] Liam O'Connor: I'll prepare a sample payload set and an infra diagram of our routing.
[36:18] Olivia Grant: I'll compile security questions and share a prioritized list.

[38:45] Diego Alvarez: One note — we'll propose a Dedicated pilot with a 2-week benchmark window and defined SLO targets to measure failover behavior.
[38:55] Sarah Patel: That works. Budget is roughly mid-four figures/month for pilot — need to confirm.

[40:12] Maya Chen: Great, we'll circulate docs by Friday. Any last questions?
[40:20] Olivia Grant: None from me.
[40:23] Liam O'Connor: All good.
[40:27] Sarah Patel: Thanks all.
[40:31] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with next steps.

End of recording.
